people.name: Eileen McMahon
bio: Eileen McMahon is a Nurse Practitioner and Clinical Educational Lead at Hannam Fertility Centre in Toronto with extensive clinical, academic, and leadership experience in reproductive health.

She earned a BA in Nursing Science, a Master's degree in Nursing, along with a post-Master's Nurse Practitioner Diploma and is an Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Toronto, where she is actively involved in education and mentorship.

Eileen served on the Board of Directors of the Canadian Fertility and Andrology Society from 2016 to 2021. She made history as CFAS's first nurse President and remains actively involved as an Executive Member of the Nursing Special Interest Group.

people.name: Sari Shaicovitch
bio: Sari Shaicovitch is a Registered Social Worker with over 25 years of clinical experience specializing in infertility, reproductive loss, perinatal mental health, anxiety, and depression.
She provides evidence-based psychotherapeutic support for individuals and couples navigating reproductive life stages and family-building challenges.

people.name: Dr. Rebecca Greenberg
bio: Dr. Rebecca Greenberg is a nurse and bioethicist with two decades of experience in healthcare. She has spent most of her career working in academic hospitals including The Hospital for Sick Children and Sinai Health, and is an Adjunct Professor at the University of Toronto.

She is committed to helping individuals and organizations navigate ethically difficult decisions. She developed and directed the Fellowship in Neonatal-Perinatal Ethics with the Toronto Centre for Neonatal Health and the University of Toronto — the first of its kind in Canada.
Dr. Greenberg is committed to education and sharing her research through speaking internationally, publishing research papers, editing books, and being featured in the media.

people.name: Dr. Ariel Dalfen
bio: Dr. Ariel Dalfen is CEO and Co-Founder of BRIA, and a psychiatrist with over 25 years of experience treating women across all reproductive life stages, from fertility through the perinatal period to perimenopause.
She co-founded BRIA after leading Ontario's largest hospital-based perinatal mental health program for 12 years and establishing Canada's first Perinatal Mental Health Telemedicine Program in 2014.
Dr. Dalfen is the author of 'When Baby Brings the Blues', serves on the Board of Directors of Fertility Matters Canada, and is an active educator and speaker on women's mental health.

people.name: Dr. Bev Young
bio: Dr. Bev Young is CMO and Co-Founder of BRIA, and a psychiatrist with over 25 years of experience in women's mental health care along with subspecialty training in adolescent psychiatry.
Before co-founding BRIA, she developed and led two of Ontario's largest perinatal psychiatry programs at Women's College Hospital and Mount Sinai Hospital.
A pioneer in virtual care since 2014, Dr. Young specializes in perimenopause and menopause mental health and serves on the Ontario Menopause Quality Standard Advisory Committee.

people.name: Michelle Amato
bio: Michelle Amato is a Registered Nurse, International Board-Certified Lactation Consultant, and BRIA Care Coordinator Manager with more than 25 years of experience in women's healthcare.
Her background includes supporting families through labor and delivery, perinatal loss, postpartum care, and lactation guidance.
She is an expert Behavioural Activation (BA) therapist and a BRIA Certified Menopause Mental Health Provider specializing in mood and anxiety care.

people.name: Nicole Schroeder
bio: Nicole Schroeder is a Registered Social Worker with post-graduate training in Emotion-Focused Therapy and sex therapy.
She specializes in sexual health, relationship dynamics, intimacy, and mental well-being during perimenopause and midlife transitions.

people.name: Lauren Rose
bio: Lauren Rose is a Registered Dietitian with over 30 years of experience in ambulatory clinical care.
She focuses on women's health nutrition, mindful eating practices, metabolic wellness, and sustainable behavior change across reproductive life stages.

people.name: Jess White
people.credentials: Therapist and Sleep Support, MA, RP
bio: Jess White is a Registered Psychotherapist and sleep specialist with advanced training in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-i).
She works with women experiencing sleep disruptions, emotional regulation challenges, and anxiety throughout pregnancy, postpartum, and perimenopause.

people.name: Amanda Thebe
bio: Amanda Thebe is a fitness and menopause educator, international speaker, and author specializing in perimenopause strength training and wellness.
She advocates for evidence-based exercise routines, stress management, and lifestyle strategies to support women through midlife hormonal transitions.

people.name: Sharon Lorber
bio: Sharon Lorber is a Registered Social Worker with over 20 years of experience supporting clients through diverse reproductive life stages.
She offers clinical counseling across life transitions, from young adulthood through pregnancy, postpartum care, and perimenopause.

people.name: Sonia Taylor
people.credentials: NP, RN (EC), Psychotherapist, MSc, BScN, NCMP
bio: Sonia Taylor is an experienced Nurse Practitioner with over 20 years of expertise in women's healthcare, certified as a menopause practitioner through NAMS.
She has delivered care in Labour & Delivery, Gynecology/Oncology, Neonatal ICU, and Primary Care.
Her clinical focus includes peri/menopause assessment, ADHD care, and integrated mental health support across the lifespan.

people.name: Dr. Maryna Mammoliti
bio: Dr. Maryna Mammoliti is a Canadian psychiatrist, educator, physician leadership expert, and internationally recognized speaker with a special interest in ADHD, physician wellness, workplace functioning, and neurodiversity.

She has focused her psychiatric practice on ADHD, PTSD, eating disorders, and physician health and wellness for the past 11 years. She has authored peer-reviewed publications and presented on ADHD across the lifespan, ADHD in physicians, and ADHD and workplace functioning.
She runs DBT skill-based groups for moms with ADHD in Ontario and Alberta and advocates for strength-based, multidisciplinary approaches to ADHD across the lifespan.

people.name: Dr. Leslie Buckley
bio: Dr. Leslie Buckley is an Addiction Psychiatrist and Chief of the Addictions Division at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH) in Toronto. Leslie completed an Addiction Psychiatry fellowship at Yale University and specializes in providing outpatient treatment for substance use disorders and concurrent disorders.

She also holds a Masters in Public Health from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Areas of interest include understanding pathways to substance use disorders as well as gender differences and the implementation of more accessible and earlier interventions in substance use health.
Dr. Buckley is an Assistant Professor at the University of Toronto, with longstanding involvement in addiction education for medical students and residents.
